nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What has been emphasized during the recent mapping exercise conducted by CHUSSDEV in Cross River State?
nodes.answer: The importance of accurate mapping to address challenges such as forest and biodiversity loss faced by the sector.
nodes.paragraph: 2020; Benefoh et al. 2018). When this study was conducted, only three studies in West Africa (Ghana and Cameroon) had been able to distinguish agrofor - estry cocoa systems from their full-sun counterparts (Ashiagbor et al. 2020; Numbisi et al. 2019; Benefoh et al. 2018). While of great scientific relevance, the methods used in those studies have limited spatial accuracy or public accessibility due to the use of com- mercial satellite imagery. This has resulted in limited applicability for cocoa land use planning (Ashiagbor et al. 2020), and understanding of the current level of climate change adaptation in Nigeria. Since this study was conducted, there have been some further developments in this area (such as Moraiti et al. 2024; Kanmegne Tamga et al. 2023). That said, mapping in Nigeria has continued to be limited. A recent map- ping exercise conducted by CHUSSDEV (2023) in Cross River State, has emphasized the importance of accurate mapping to address challenges such as forest and biodiversity loss faced by the sector.

nodes.question: What distance were the study sites located from protected area (PA) boundaries compared to the mean across the study region?
nodes.answer: The study sites were located 35 km away from PA boundaries, compared to a mean distance of 48 km across the study region.
nodes.paragraph: Across all studies, hunters sold a mean of 57 17% of the animals hunted (range, 17 94%). The studies were biased towards areas with greater forest cover: the mean forest cover within 20 km of sites was 90 8% (Fig. 1 ), whereas the mean forest cover across the study region was 50 33%. The study sites were located closer to protected area (PA) boundaries (35 30 km away) compared with the mean across the study region of 48 km (excluding points inside PAs), and in areas with lower human population density (7 13 individuals per km2) than the mean across the study region of 40 86 individuals per km2 in 2020 (excluding urban areas).
